reply.text:
Counting every calorie and panicking when you go over is a hard place to be, and I'm glad you said it out loud. Training can help your relationship with food in some ways. Lifting builds strength and muscle, and steady sessions give you structure and a sense of progress that isn't just the number on the scale or the food log. It won't make the counting itself stop, though, and I'm not the right person to tell you how much to eat or whether the counting is hurting you.

If the panic is getting in the way of eating, sleeping or enjoying your training, that's one to talk through with a doctor or a dietitian who works with eating concerns. They can give you the real answer, and I'll keep building your training around whatever they and you decide.

In the meantime, I can help keep the gym side steady: consistent sessions, progression you can see, and rest days that count too. Want me to look at how your training has been going lately?
